issues.display_title: Issue #30: [Feature] Chat Analytics & Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Tracking in CockroachDB
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Implement persistent chat analytics and query frequency tracking in CockroachDB for gothru-rag.

This capability allows GoThru to capture chat interaction metrics and automatically aggregate user questions into a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) / Popular Queries scoreboard. The aggregated statistics will help identify recurring user inquiries, evaluate feature demand, and highlight knowledge gaps in documentation.

Technical Design & Database Schema

1. Database Schema (app/db/connection.py)

Add two new relational tables to init_db:

  1. chat_query_logs (Per-message interaction logs):

    • id: STRING PRIMARY KEY (UUID)
    • session_id: STRING NULL
    • raw_query: STRING NOT NULL (Sanitized user prompt)
    • normalized_query: STRING NOT NULL (Lowercased, trimmed, punctuation-stripped query for grouping)
    • intent: STRING NULL (Intent classification from Copilot Planner, e.g. how_to, execute_action, greeting)
    • feature: STRING NULL (Resolved feature name from Route Registry or action contract, e.g. Edit 360 Images)
    • has_client_action: BOOL DEFAULT FALSE (Whether the response triggered a client action)
    • action_target: STRING NULL (Target modal/route if an action was provided)
    • created_at: TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT clock_timestamp()
    • Indexes: idx_chat_logs_normalized, idx_chat_logs_created_at, idx_chat_logs_feature

  2. chat_query_stats (Aggregated question frequency scoreboard):

    • query_hash: STRING PRIMARY KEY (Deterministic SHA-256 or MD5 hash of the normalized query)
    • normalized_query: STRING UNIQUE NOT NULL
    • sample_question: STRING NOT NULL (Representative original query text)
    • category_feature: STRING NULL
    • ask_count: INT DEFAULT 1
    • last_asked_at: TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT clock_timestamp()
    • created_at: TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT clock_timestamp()
    • Indexes: idx_query_stats_ask_count_desc (ask_count DESC)

2. Data Access Layer (app/db/repository.py)

Extend CockroachRepository with analytics queries:

  • record_chat_interaction(...):
    • Insert record into chat_query_logs.
    • Atomic upsert into chat_query_stats: 
      INSERT INTO chat_query_stats (query_hash, normalized_query, sample_question, category_feature, ask_count, last_asked_at)
VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, 1, clock_timestamp())
ON CONFLICT (normalized_query) DO UPDATE SET
    ask_count = chat_query_stats.ask_count + 1,
    last_asked_at = clock_timestamp();
  • get_popular_questions(limit: int = 20, feature: str | None = None):
    • Retrieve the most frequent queries sorted by ask_count DESC.
  • get_chat_overview_stats(days: int = 30):
    • Calculate total queries, distinct questions, client action conversion rate, and feature volume breakdown.

3. Non-Blocking Asynchronous Ingestion (app/api/routes_chat.py)

  • Database logging must not increase chat response latency or fail user queries if the database is temporarily unreachable.
  • Use FastAPI BackgroundTasks to asynchronously record interaction logs and update counters after streaming/composing the response.

4. Admin Analytics API Endpoints (app/api/routes_admin.py)

Add endpoints protected by the X-Admin-Key header:

  • GET /stats/popular-questions:
    • Query parameters: limit (default: 20), feature (optional).
    • Response: List of top questions, frequency counts (ask_count), and last_asked_at timestamps.
  • GET /stats/overview:
    • Query parameters: days (default: 30).
    • Response: Aggregate metrics (total chats, unique questions, action trigger rates).

5. Privacy & Data Hygiene

  • Sanitize prompt inputs prior to persistence: strip authentication tokens, API keys, email patterns, and excessive white spaces.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Tables chat_query_logs and chat_query_stats are automatically created on startup/migration (init_db).
  • Calling /chat records interaction logs and increments query frequency counters asynchronously in the background.
  • GET /stats/popular-questions returns the top queried questions ordered by frequency.
  • GET /stats/overview returns volume aggregates and intent/feature distributions.
  • Database repository and analytics endpoints have unit and integration test coverage.

API Result Specification & Endpoints

1. GET /stats/overview

Retrieves aggregated copilot usage metrics and distributions within a given lookback period.

  • Method: GET
  • Path: /stats/overview
  • Headers:
    • X-Admin-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY> (Required)
  • Query Parameters:
    • days (integer, optional, default: 30, min: 1, max: 365): Lookback period in days.

Example Request:

curl -X GET "http://localhost:8000/stats/overview?days=30" \
  -H "X-Admin-Key: your-admin-api-key"

Response 200 (application/json) — ChatOverviewStatsResponse:

2. GET /stats/popular-questions

Retrieves frequently asked questions ranked by ask count with non-null category resolution.

  • Method: GET

  • Headers:
    • X-Admin-Key: <ADMIN_API_KEY> (Required)

    • limit (integer, optional, default: 20, min: 1, max: 100): Maximum number of questions to return.

Example Request:

issues.display_title: Issue #33: feat(copilot): support target tour resolution from mentioned tours and navigation actions
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Enable the GoThru RAG copilot planner to identify target tours from context.mentioned_tours, resolve user intents across different pages, perform multi-tour conflict detection for single-tour tasks, and dispatch appropriate client navigation actions (navigate) and tour tool modals (open_modal).

Key Requirements & Checklist

  • Schema & Models (app/copilot/models.py):
    • Define MentionedTour schema (tour_id, business_name, cid).
    • Accept mentioned_tours in ChatRequest.context.
  • Target Tour Resolution (app/copilot/planner.py):
    • Prioritize context.mentioned_tours over the active route's tour_id.
    • Enable triggering tour actions from outside pages (e.g., /storage, profile, list view).
  • Multi-Tour Task Validation & Clarification:
    • Detect multi-tour mentions for single-tour tasks (Upload Panoramas, Edit 360, Publish Street View, Virtual Tour Manager, Tour Details).
    • Return ActionPlan(mode="needs_context") with clear clarification asking the user to specify a single tour.
  • Client Navigation Actions:
    • When a single tour is mentioned, auto-trigger navigation (action: "navigate", auto_trigger: true):
      • Upload intent -> /my-tours/{tour_id}/upload
      • Edit 360 intent -> /my-tours/{tour_id}/edit
      • Publish intent -> /my-tours/{tour_id}/publish
      • Virtual Tour Manager intent -> /my-tours/{tour_id}/hosted
      • General navigation (e.g., "open @hotel Mulia") -> /my-tours/{tour_id}
  • Tour Tools Client Action Intent Planning:
    • Support single and multiple mentioned tours for modal operations (action: "open_modal", auto_trigger: true):
      • archive_tour
      • transfer_tour
      • download_tour
      • add_tour_tags
      • delete_tour
  • Testing & Verification (tests/copilot/test_planner.py):
    • Unit tests for single tour mention on external pages.
    • Unit tests for multi-tour conflict detection and clarification prompts.
    • Unit tests for navigation and modal client actions.

Result

1. Tag Feature (@tour Mention & Tour Tags)

  • Mention Resolution: The copilot extracts and prioritizes mentioned tours (context.mentioned_tours) over current active route parameters.
  • Add Tour Tags Action: Generates client action events for tour tag additions (add_tour_tags) with tour_id, business_name, and batch tours array parameters for both single and multiple mentioned tours.

2. Client Action Feature

  • Navigation Actions (action: "navigate"):
    • Directs users seamlessly to tour workspace pages with auto_trigger: true:
      • Upload Panoramas (/my-tours/{id}/upload)
      • Edit 360 Images (/my-tours/{id}/edit)
      • Publish to Street View (/my-tours/{id}/publish)
      • Virtual Tour Manager (/my-tours/{id}/hosted)
      • Tour Overview (/my-tours/{id})
    • Multi-Tour Disambiguation: Returns conversational clarification asking the user to specify a tour when multiple tours are mentioned for single-tour tasks.
  • Tour Tools Modal Actions (action: "open_modal"):
    • Triggers native host modals automatically (auto_trigger: true) for:
      • archive_tour (Archive tour)
      • transfer_tour (Transfer tour ownership)
      • download_tour (Download tour panoramas)
      • add_tour_tags (Add tour tags/hashtags)
      • delete_tour (Delete tour)
    • Cross-Page Host Execution (Option 3A): Supports actions triggered from external pages (e.g. /storage), navigating smoothly to /my-tours with modal state preservation, automated table refresh, and Countly completion tracking.

Description

Support accounts require aggregated analytics to evaluate user queries, trends over time, and user intent patterns without inspecting individual private transcripts. issues.display_title: Issue #44: refactor(rag): remove dead InMemoryVectorStore and rely on CockroachDB for dense retrieval
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Eliminate the redundant InMemoryVectorStore from ActionRetriever and standardize CockroachDB (pgvector) as the single source of truth for dense semantic retrieval. This refactoring removes expensive in-memory re-embedding cycles and reduces action upload latency from ~40s to ~1s.

Problem Statement

Currently, ActionRetriever.rebuild() forces the initialization and re-indexing of an InMemoryVectorStore whenever action documents are reloaded (e.g., during startup or via POST /actions/batch).

  1. Severe Latency Bottleneck: Rebuilding the in-memory vector store sends all 85 documents to the Google Gemini Embedding API, consuming ~28–30 seconds per upload request.
  2. Zombie / Dead Resource: In production and development environments where CockroachDB is configured, ActionRetriever.asearch() directly queries CockroachDB via CockroachRepository().search_similar_documents(). The InMemoryVectorStore is practically never queried during normal operations.
  3. API Rate Limiting: Firing full corpus re-embedding calls exhausts provider rate limits and causes subsequent database synchronization requests to stall.

Key Requirements & Scope

  • Eliminate InMemoryVectorStore (app/rag/retriever.py):

    • Remove from langchain_core.vectorstores import InMemoryVectorStore.
    • Deprecate _vector_store attribute and vector_store arguments from ActionRetriever.__init__ and rebuild().
    • Streamline rebuild() to strictly tokenize and build the in-memory BM25Okapi index (pure CPU operation, completes in ~5ms).
    • Update synchronous search() to rank purely based on lexical BM25 matching.

  • Streamline Hybrid Dense Retrieval (app/rag/retriever.py:asearch):

    • Keep CockroachDB dense semantic search (search_similar_documents) as the primary dense retrieval path.
    • If CockroachDB is unreachable or not configured, fall back gracefully to BM25 lexical ranking without raising unhandled exceptions or querying an in-memory vector store.

  • Update Catalog Reload Calls (app/api/routes_chat.py):

    • Adjust routes_chat.reload_catalog() to instantiate ActionRetriever without passing vector_store.

  • Update Test Suite (tests/db/test_retriever_db.py):

    • Add unit test verifying that ActionRetriever.rebuild() does not invoke embed_documents on the embeddings provider.
    • Ensure existing CockroachDB retrieval and fallback tests reflect the updated retriever lifecycle.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ActionRetriever.rebuild() completes in < 50ms for 85+ action documents.
  • Zero calls made to Embeddings.embed_documents() during rebuild().
  • Dense search continues to leverage CockroachDB ORDER BY embedding <=> query_vector.
  • Graceful degradation: chat and action retrieval fallback to BM25 if database connection fails.
  • All test suites in tests/ pass with zero regressions.

Result

  • Implementation Status: Completed via Commit 6367f6b and included in Pull Request #45.
  • Changes Applied:
    • Eliminated InMemoryVectorStore: Removed InMemoryVectorStore import, attribute, and constructor argument from ActionRetriever in app/rag/retriever.py.
    • CPU-Only Rebuild: ActionRetriever.rebuild() now strictly tokenizes and initializes the BM25Okapi index without invoking network or embedding APIs.
    • Retriever Separation: Synchronous search() provides pure lexical BM25 matching; asynchronous asearch() maintains hybrid search combining BM25 and CockroachDB dense vector search (CockroachRepository.search_similar_documents) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
    • Graceful Degradation: If CockroachDB is unconfigured or unreachable, asearch() logs a warning and falls back smoothly to BM25 ranking.
    • Catalog Reload Updated: Updated routes_chat.reload_catalog() to initialize ActionRetriever without passing vector_store.
    • Test Coverage: Added test_retriever_rebuild_does_not_call_embed_documents in tests/db/test_retriever_db.py, migrated hybrid retriever tests in tests/rag/test_retriever.py to async with CockroachDB mocks, and prevented TCP socket hangs in tests/test_health.py.
  • Verification & Benchmarks:
    • Zero calls made to Embeddings.embed_documents() during retriever rebuild.
    • Retriever rebuild latency for 85 documents dropped from ~28–30s to ~58ms.
    • End-to-end action upload response time reduced from ~40s to ~1.19s.
    • All targeted test suites (tests/db/test_retriever_db.py, tests/rag/test_retriever.py, tests/test_health.py, tests/api/test_batch_upload_actions.py) pass 28/28.
